_readme: City guide for the office cities. Keys are 'City|ST'. Facts must come from a source you can link. Photos load from Wikimedia Commons by file name; fill in credit and license from the file page and set verified to true. A city without an entry still works: the app shows its data and a drawn placeholder instead of a photo.

Fishers|IN.summary: A fast-growing suburb northeast of Indianapolis, built around trails, a reservoir and an outdoor concert series.

facts.text: About 99,000 residents in the 2020 census.
The city center is 16 miles northeast of downtown Indianapolis.
25 parks and nature preserves, and more than 131 miles of trails and greenways.
Geist Reservoir is used for fishing and waterskiing.
Symphony on the Prairie is a summer concert series at Conner Prairie.
Public schools are run by Hamilton Southeastern Schools, which serves almost 21,000 students.

Overland Park|KS.summary: The largest city in Johnson County, Kansas, south of Kansas City, with a large park system and a 300-acre arboretum.

facts.text: About 197,000 residents in the 2020 census, the largest city in Johnson County.
The city center is about 13 miles south-southwest of downtown Kansas City, Missouri.
84 parks covering more than 1,800 acres of park land and open space.
The Overland Park Arboretum and Botanical Gardens covers 300 acres.
Oak Park Mall has nearly 200 stores.
T-Mobile was the city's largest employer in its 2016 report, with 6,300 employees.

photo.alt: 95th Street and Metcalf Avenue at sunset

Frisco|TX.summary: A Dallas–Fort Worth city known for its pro sports venues, including the Dallas Cowboys' headquarters.

facts.text: About 200,500 residents in the 2020 census.
Part of the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex, about 25 miles from both Dallas Love Field and DFW Airport.
The Star is the Dallas Cowboys' headquarters, with the 12,000-seat Ford Center.
Toyota Stadium (20,500 seats) is home to FC Dallas, and the National Soccer Hall of Fame is here.
The Frisco Athletic Center has about 18,000 sq ft of indoor and 40,000 sq ft of outdoor pools.
Stonebriar Centre is a regional mall with about 165 stores.

photo.alt: George A. Purefoy Municipal Center at Frisco Square

Naperville|IL.summary: A riverside city in the western Chicago suburbs with a downtown Riverwalk and a large park district.

facts.text: About 149,500 residents in the 2020 census, Illinois' fourth-largest city.
About 28 miles southwest of Chicago on the DuPage River, with Metra and Amtrak service.
The Riverwalk runs about 1.75 miles along the West Branch of the DuPage River.
Centennial Beach is a former quarry turned into a swimming beach.
The Naperville Park District manages over 2,400 acres, 136 parks and 70 miles of trails.

photo.alt: Moser Tower and Rotary Hill over the Riverwalk quarry

Ann Arbor|MI.summary: Home of the University of Michigan, with a walkable downtown and more than 160 city parks.

facts.text: About 124,000 residents in the 2020 census, Michigan's fifth-largest city.
Home to the University of Michigan, which employs about 30,000 people.
More than 160 city parks.
The Michigan Theater hosts the Ann Arbor Film Festival and the Ann Arbor Symphony.
Ranked first among U.S. cities for booksellers and books sold per person.
Part of the Greater Detroit combined statistical area.
